label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 127.

diagnosis.hypothesis: A poison message is blocking the ledger. Provider event evt_000282 (provider-events partition 1, offset 129) carries an invalid amount: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. At 20:31:21 ledger-consumer was redeployed with BAD_EVENTS=retry. Under that setting it retries the same message forever, with backoff capped at 15 s, and never commits past offset 129. Every later message on partition 1 queues behind it, so ledger lag climbs, the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff, and the BooksBehindProvider alert fires. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. It dead-lettered the same event and kept going, which is why only the ledger is behind. Still open: why the event's amount is invalid (the provider sent a bad payload, or the receiver mangled it; I did not inspect the payload), and what BAD_EVENTS was before the deploy (most likely dead_letter, which I infer but have not verified).

evidence.shows: Consumer lag rose from 0 at 20:30:31 to 1 at 20:31:31 and to 177 at 20:32:31.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 20:31:21Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1＠129 on attempts 3 through 9, with backoff growing to 15 s: 'amount must be positive integer cents'.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message (provider-events/1＠129) at 20:31:23 for the same invalid-amount reason, then moved on.

Trace for evt_000282: the receiver queued it at partition 1, offset 129. The ledger tried it 12 times over 75 s, every attempt with outcome will_retry and an error. The confirmer's outcome was dead_lettered.

The ledger still posts events at about 1/s, presumably from other partitions, while the confirmer logs a dead_lettered outcome. This fits one partition being stuck rather than the whole consumer failing.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 20:31:21 deploy, so a bad event is dead-lettered instead of retried forever and partition 1 can drain. Afterwards, look at evt_000282 in the dead-letter topic, find out why its amount is invalid, and book it by hand or repair it once it is understood. Then run the money check to confirm the books have caught up.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer is recreated, so ledger booking pauses briefly during the restart. If the previous setting dead-letters bad events, evt_000282 will be missing from the ledger until someone books it by hand, and the money check will flag it until then. If the previous setting was not dead_letter, the rollback may not unblock the partition.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). The handler is idempotent, so replaying events is safe.
